risk_assessment.rationale: The 37 scanning events from IP 52.14.201.133 and domains united-telco.com/victimcorp.com are observed; no evidence of successful email delivery or execution, and the IP/domains are not known malicious.

recommended_actions: Escalate to a human analyst for manual review
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Deploy a temporary block on outbound SMTP traffic from the IP address 52.14.201.133 until further analysis confirms its legitimacy.

Add the sender domain united‑telco.com to the organization’s phishing whitelist only after verifying that it is a legitimate billing partner; otherwise, treat all messages from this domain as suspicious and route them through the advanced threat protection engine.

Enable detailed logging for any future emails with the subject line pattern ‘Your * bill is ready’ so that you can correlate delivery attempts with user interactions (e.g., link clicks or attachment downloads).

Conduct a quick internal survey asking finance staff whether they have received legitimate invoices from United‑Telco in the past month; any positive confirmation should trigger an immediate review of the sender’s certificate and DKIM/SPF alignment.
Run a sandbox analysis on the email’s attachments (if any) and embedded URLs to confirm that no malicious payloads are present before allowing them through to end users.

Set up a honeypot mailbox for finance@victimcorp.com that mimics the real inbox but logs all inbound traffic; this will help determine whether the bulk messages actually reach legitimate recipients or are simply part of a reconnaissance sweep.
Coordinate with Mimecast’s support team to request a deeper forensic analysis of the message header and any associated delivery reports, focusing on the 37 scanning events that were logged.
triage_rationale_experimental: The alert shows typical bulk‑phishing characteristics but lacks definitive compromise evidence; further investigation is required to determine if it is a genuine threat or a false alarm.
